summary: Replaced the 36 seeded research targets with the 8 real partners
body:
The seeded list (Swiss Re, Munich Re, Fermat, Dialog Axiata and the rest) was never contacted — every record sat at Identified with `seeded: true`. All 36 removed; git history keeps them. In their place: the real partner list, with stages taken from the status column — signed → MoU signed, send → MoU sent, need to be aligned → Researched.

Seventeen plan tasks pointed at deleted partners. Two Sri Lanka regulatory tasks (t303, t305) were repointed to the new Sri Lanka record; the other fifteen had their partner link cleared and need reattaching.

summary: Confirm the spelling and the signing entity
body: Entered as "Hakuhodo Key3" — the source list read "Hakahudo Key3", which looks like a typo for the Hakuhodo × Key3 joint venture. Confirm the spelling and the exact legal entity on the signed MoU.
"Sumitomo Insurance" is ambiguous — Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance (MS&AD) and Sumitomo Life are different houses with different appetites. Confirm which one holds the MoU before any follow-up goes out.

summary: Which Sumitomo entity runs the web3 activity?
body: Recorded as the digital-asset arm of the Sumitomo group. Confirm the entity name and whether it is the same counterparty as the insurance MoU or a separate one.

summary: "Sri Lanka" — which body is the counterparty?
body: Held as a single public-sector record for the host country. The alignment question is which body actually signs: the Insurance Regulatory Commission, the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission, the Central Bank, the Disaster Management Centre, or a ministry above them. Tasks t303 and t305 are attached here until that is settled — split the record once it is.
Write proxy is live. The desk now commits through it, so browsers hold a team password instead of a GitHub token; the token stays on the server.

Replaced the 39 seeded tasks with 13 real ones. The seeded plan assumed week zero — shortlist operators, first discovery meeting, operator MoU signed in December — while the board already showed one MoU signed and three sent. The new tasks come from that reality: the four open entity questions, follow-ups on the three MoUs out, and next steps for ADB, Aon and Vodafone. The old plan is in git history. Board columns are now Backlog / Weekly / Focus / Review / Done, matching the workforce board. No task has an owner yet.
Researched → MoU sent
MoU sent → Aligning MoU
Researched → Meeting held
Researched → Aligning MoU
Meeting held → Aligning MoU

Removed six tasks that the MoU cards now track: the three MoU follow-ups (Sumitomo Insurance, Sumitomo Web3, Mobily) and the three approach tasks for ADB, Aon and Vodafone, all of whom are already in conversation. Seven tasks remain, none of which is an MoU state.

Cleared all 7 tasks at your request. Every one of them was inferred by me from the partner records rather than written by you. The MoUs remain — they are derived from the partner stages, not invented. The removed list is in git history: Confirm the legal entity on the signed Hakuhodo Key3 MoU; Establish which Sumitomo entity the insurance MoU went to — Mitsui Sumitomo or Sumitomo Life; Confirm Sumitomo Web3 is the counterparty entity, not a group description; Establish which Sri Lankan body is the counterparty and can sign; Define what Hakuhodo Key3 actually does in the facility now the MoU is signed; Bring the MoU template to counsel — three are already out and one is signed; List what each MoU commits us to, signed and sent

Cleared the six seeded milestones. They described a later phase - term sheet, capital indication, regulatory pathway, go-live - while the work in front of the project is getting the MoUs signed and the partners aligned. One of them, 'Operator MoU signed' dated 19 Dec, already contradicted a signed MoU on the board. In git history: Operator MoU signed (2026-12-19); Term sheet v1 issued (2027-01-16); Capital indication received (2027-02-27); Regulatory pathway confirmed (2027-03-27); Sponsor funding secured (2027-04-30); Facility go-live decision (2027-06-30)

Added as an advisor / introducer at Toni's request. Role not recorded — named without a stated reason, and nothing has been invented to fill the gap. Surname spelling also unconfirmed. Both need answering before this record is used in outreach.
Added as an advisor / introducer at Toni's request, to help reach investors. The specific investors and the introduction ask are still open.

Added an 'Advisors & introducers' partner type. The nine existing types are all institutions — a carrier, a fund, a regulator. These two records are people, and putting a person under 'Capital providers' would have said something untrue about what they are. Note this is the first time the board holds named private individuals rather than organisations, in a public repository.

Split the people types in two: Advisors and Network. Toni corrected an earlier lump-them-together call — Siva advises, Roland and Seena are network. The difference is what you ask for: an advisor tells you what is wrong with the thing, a network contact tells you who to show it to, and the outreach templates now differ accordingly. Roland and Seena were moved from advisor to network.
Aligning MoU → MoU sent

Put Toni's nine current items on the board, grouped by workstream. Focus holds one thing — catching up on the MoUs — because that is the stated headline problem. Weekly holds the four that are dated or feed something dated. The rest are in Backlog with no invented deadlines.
Added a tenth workstream, Company & governance. The nine that existed all build the facility; the commercial model, the UK charity and Siva's role build the company, and had nowhere to sit.

Overlaps LC-013 on the workforce board, "Create slides for Scott Petty VF CTO for Sri Lanka pilot", which is in Focus there. Kept separate because this one carries the meeting dates and is broader than the slides, but they may want merging.
Likely overlaps LC-014 on the workforce board, "Send to Matthew pack", which is already in Review there. Created because Toni listed it explicitly; delete whichever is the duplicate.
Added at Toni's request as "ethereum institutional team". Category guessed as digital-asset infrastructure — not stated. Entity, contact and the ask are all open.
Added at Toni's request. Filed as a donor since a donation fund is a philanthropic funder. Which of the two Ethereum records Matthew Dawson belongs to is open.
Identified → Approached

Added an Outreach material workstream at Toni's request. It overlaps WS9 Narrative & materials, which currently holds "Update the pitch deck" and "Update the website" — the deck in particular is outreach material by any reading. Left both where they are rather than moving someone else's work between groups unasked.

Added Manila invite and Charity setup as workstreams at Toni's request, and moved the two tasks named after them across: Align the ADB invite — Manila, 21–24 Sept: WS8 -> WS12; Set up the UK charity: WS10 -> WS13. Worth noting there are now thirteen workstreams for nine tasks — more groups than things grouped. That is fine while the streams are being sketched out, but if most stay empty the grouping stops carrying information.

Removed WS10 Company & governance. Toni pointed out it was never asked for — I invented it while putting their nine items on the board because three of them did not fit the existing nine, which was my call to make and it was not mine. The two tasks left in it went back to workstreams that already existed: the commercial model to Capital & structure, Siva's role to Funding & partnerships. Both are my guesses at the least-wrong home, not decisions Toni made.

Added a workstream called Tasks and moved everything I had placed by guesswork into it. Toni named three workstreams — Outreach material, Manila invite, UK charity — and the only two placements they actually stated were the tasks those workstreams are named after. The other seven had been filed into WS1-WS9 on my judgement of where they fitted, which was not asked for. They now sit in Tasks until Toni says otherwise.
Moved the pitch deck and the website into Outreach material at Toni's instruction. Used the existing WS11 rather than creating a second workstream of the same name.

Renamed "Sri Lanka" to Colombo UrbanLab. This answers the open question on this record about which Sri Lankan body it stands for. Only the name was changed — the category, the why and the ask still describe the country placeholder and need rewriting to match the organisation.

Added at Toni's request as "World Bank with Fundschain", kept as one record in their own words rather than guessing at a split. Category inferred as development finance. Whether this is one joint approach or two counterparties is open.

Researched the four events. Two have public pages and now carry links: Digital Insurance CEE (digital-insurance-cee.com, dates confirmed as 8-9 Sept, Warsaw) and the ADB Business Opportunities Fair (adb.org, confirmed 21-24 Sept at ADB HQ Manila, 09:00-17:30 local, with venue and times filled in from that page). The Scott Petty meeting is private. The HT Digital & Aon roundtable has no public listing — Aon's own events pages do not carry it — so it is treated as invite-only; only the Aon Centre street address was added, from aon.com. Both links were checked live before being saved.

Moved to 24 August on Toni's word, from "Prepare the Vodafone CTO meeting (Scott Petty), 27–28 Aug" due 2026-08-27. That settles the contradiction flagged when the event was added — the task and the event now agree. Still outstanding: LC-013 on the workforce board reads "27 Aug 26" and lives in the other repository, so it was not touched from here.
Last contact 25 Aug: update received from them. Recorded from Toni's account, wording his.
Last contact 25 Aug: meeting on Tuesday. Stage left at MoU sent — a meeting while the MoU is out does not move it on its own.
Last contact 12 Aug. Two weeks quiet with the MoU out — the oldest of the three sent.
Last contact 19 Aug, with the MoU out.
Last contact Friday 21 Aug.
Last contact Monday 24 Aug — talked at the beginning of the week.
Last contact 25 Aug.
Approached today, 26 Aug. Second meeting booked for 2 September, now the due date on the record.
Researched → Approached

Added at Toni's request alongside the Vodafone operator record. Recorded as a foundation, so Donors & foundations rather than Infrastructure operators. Why them, who the contact is, and whether it runs through the same relationship as the operator conversation are all still open — none of it has been invented.

Partners table now shows Last contact where it showed Owner. Owner was unassigned on every one of the sixteen records, so the column carried nothing; when a conversation was last touched is the thing you actually scan for. The owner field is untouched and still in the editor. Eight dates entered from Toni's account; the other eight records have no last contact recorded and show a dash rather than a guess.

MoU sent → MoU signed. Signed today, 26 Aug. Next move was "Chase countersignature", which is now done; replaced with the same next move the other signed MoU carries — define scope and first deliverable. That wording is mirrored from Hakuhodo Key3, not something you said, so correct it if the actual next step differs.
Approached → MoU signed. Signed today, 26 Aug, without passing through the intermediate stages — approached and signed on the same day. The 2 September meeting stands and is still the due date.

The long-standing question on this record — which Sri Lankan body is the counterparty and can sign — is answered in practice: Colombo UrbanLab signed. What that does not settle is whether an urban policy organisation is the counterparty the facility needs for the public-sector side, or whether a regulator or ministry is still required alongside it.

Still open from before signature: this record is filed under Regulators & public bodies, and its "why" and "ask" still describe the country rather than this organisation. Worth rewriting now that there is a signed MoU behind the name.
Two MoUs signed today, taking the count from one to three: Hakuhodo Key3, Mobily, Colombo UrbanLab. Three remain out — Sumitomo Insurance, Sumitomo Web3, Aon.

Removed two records at Toni's request: Siva Balasuriyar (advisor) and David Palmer (network). Taken with them, because they pointed at nothing once the records were gone: task t108 "Confirm how Siva is involved in the project", and two log entries that referenced the records directly. Deleting log entries goes against the append-only rule in AGENTS.md — done here only because the removal was asked for directly, and leaving entries whose whole subject is a named private individual would have defeated the point. Passing mentions of both names survive in other board-level entries, and git history holds everything regardless: removing a name from the working copy does not remove it from a public repository's past.

Added an Investors tab and 67 investor records — the investor space for the $8.5M seed. Two sources, kept apart by the source field on each record: the two curated sheets of a third-party fundraising workbook (imported in full, firm names only; that project's outreach statuses, contacts and 256-name universe deliberately left out), and research on 4 September into who funded the precedents in this category — Descartes, Arbol, FloodFlash, Raincoat, IBISA, Ledger Investing, Re, OnRe, Birch Hill. Tiered A/B/C for an $8.5M seed rather than the pre-seed the workbook assumed: 18 A, 33 B, 16 C. Every record starts at Identified; nothing from anyone else's pipeline was carried over as a status.

MS&AD Ventures is the corporate venture arm of MS&AD — the group behind Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance. If the Sumitomo Insurance MoU (p02) sits with Mitsui Sumitomo, this is the investing arm of a counterparty already at MoU stage, and the warmest strategic on the list. If it sits with Sumitomo Life, the warm path is Anthemis instead, whose new insurance fund has Sumitomo Life as an LP. The open question on p02 now has a fundraising consequence.

The workbook ranked SiriusPoint #8 and called it 'THE strategic slot'. That is stale: the current CEO is on record reducing equity stakes in MGAs and taking an underwriting-first approach, and the last venture deal found is December 2024. Re-tiered to B. Still worth a conversation — as fronting or capacity, not as an equity cheque.

ADB Ventures funds parametric insurtech in Asia — IBISA's $3M round in 2024, with Acumen and Equator — and ADB itself is aligning on the facility. The Business Opportunities Fair in Manila, 21–24 September, puts both the partner and the investor in one building. Worth deciding before then whether the ask to ADB is a country-programme conversation, a venture conversation, or both.

Investors tab rebuilt after Toni's feedback: the view read as a pipeline — stage, last contact, due — for a raise where all 67 are still at Identified, the tier was explained only in a footnote, the 'why' was hidden in a hover, and the order within a tier was alphabetical, which looked like a priority and was not. Now: grouped by tier with the rule in each header; an explicit rank inside each tier — a path in through something already on this board first, then funds that can lead a round this size, then the freshest dated evidence; each row shows why, the evidence with a source link, the path in and the ask. Every fund has a website link checked live (61) or an honest 'search' link (6) — never a guessed URL. 47 evidence lines carry the article they came from. SiriusPoint's demotion now rests on The Insurer: the CEO has ruled out future MGA equity investments.

Investors tab tidied after Toni's second round: the list had become a wall of five-line rows in two fonts, and clicking a fund opened a form with three-line boxes you could not read. Now a row is one line to scan — rank, name with a link, type and place, and who they backed — and a click opens the case as paragraphs: why they fit, the evidence with its source, precedents, path in, ask, notes, with Edit as a button. The CRM block — owner, contact, next move, due, last contact — is gone from the editor, the data, the schema and the contract: this is a map of the space, not a pipeline, and all sixty-seven were empty anyway. Stage stays as a chip because the Overview reads it.

Investors list restructured as a decision table at Toni's request: #, Investor with its website, the Evidence in full, the Year of its latest dated deal, and the Source link — so funds can be compared in the list without opening anything. Year is a new field, derived once from the dates already in each evidence line (67 records; 8 undated, all workbook entries marked 'not verified'), editable beside rank. The why, precedents, path in and ask stay in the profile.
